candidates.title: Adaptive Electromagnetic Transient-level Digital Twins for Data Centers via In-Context Learning with LLMs
candidates.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads has significantly increased data center (DC) power demand. Frequent operational and configurational changes, such as load surges caused by dynamic workload allocation, can induce electromagnetic transients (EMTs) whose accurate prediction is critical for reliable DC operation and maintenance. Although high-fidelity EMT solvers are widely adopted for transient analysis, their computational cost limits large-scale and multi-scenario studies. Digital twins address this computational bottleneck by emulating the behavior of a physical system and enabling fast prediction in place of expensive high-fidelity simulation. However,data-driven digital twins are non-adaptive and fail to generalize once the DC configuration changes. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an adaptive EMT-level digital twin for DCs based on in-context learning (ICL) with large language models (LLMs). We formulate the EMT prediction task as a system identification problem under parametric uncertainty and develop a GPT-2-based framework that adapts to unseen DC configurations at inference time from a small set of EMT trajectory samples, without model retraining. The proposed framework is validated on three representative EMT scenarios and benchmarked against three baseline non-adaptive twins. Results demonstrate superior prediction accuracy, improved adaptability to unseen operating conditions, and substantial computational speedups compared to high-fidelity EMT simulation.

candidates.title: Measurement Artifacts in Trustworthiness Evaluations of Quantized Small Language Models
candidates.abstract: Evaluations of quantized language models attribute the change in a benchmark score to quantization. We write the measured change as the true change plus a term contributed by the instrument. Instrument error that is the same at every precision can shrink a paired comparison but cannot create or reverse an effect. Error that interacts with quantization can do both, and it is reported as an effect of quantization. We estimate this interaction for four measurement choices in 8 instruction-tuned models below two billion parameters, at float16, LLM.int8() and NF4, on identical items. Measured against labels from two human annotators, the 4-bit rise in harmful compliance is about half to two-thirds of the rise in non-refusal that a corrected key word detector records. Cloze and lettered multiple-choice scoring disagree about the effect of quantization far more than their noise allows: their estimates correlate at \r{ho} = 0.10, against a ceiling of about 0.77. LLM.int8() answers and generations depend on which items share a batch, and padding alone changes its answers. Rounding activations to 8 bits is enough to produce this dependence. NF4 is batch-invariant. The two largest reported calibration losses are response-bias shifts. We release item-level predictions, option scores and human annotations, and give recommendations for evaluating compressed small models.

candidates.title: Cosmological Constant Screening from Quantum Horizon Chaos
candidates.abstract: We propose a microscopic mechanism for screening the cosmological constant through quantum chaos of the horizon degrees of freedom. We show that in a recently proposed quantum-horizon matrix model arXiv:2406.01466, the Schwarzschild--de Sitter junction completion arXiv:2608.21178 supports a gravitationally dressed soft mode that approaches the massless minimally coupled scalar of de Sitter gravity. Interactions among the microscopic horizon degrees of freedom provide a mechanism for force relaxation. Assuming a finite-memory force spectrum with nonzero regular low-frequency weight, the gravitationally dressed soft mode undergoes Brownian diffusion after momentum relaxation. The resulting bosonic coarse-grained entropy supplements the background entropy arising from fermionic parton microstates. We propose that their sum defines the total thermodynamic entropy, which can be identified with the Gibbons--Hawking entropy of the backreacted causal horizon. Entropy generation during the diffusion regime then leads to infrared screening of the effective cosmological constant, with a universal entropy--variance coefficient agreeing with that of Kitazawa and collaborators. Radiative lifting of the soft mode provides a possible mechanism for terminating the screening regime.

candidates.title: Teichmüller spaces with conical singularities and Virasoro coadjoint orbits
candidates.abstract: We study Teichmüller spaces of hyperbolic \(0\)-metrics on a disk with ideal boundary and a marked point carrying a conical singularity with angle $θ= 2πβ$. For all $β>0$, we show that $\rm{Teich}^β(\overline{\mathbb D})\cong S^1\backslash \rm{Diff}(S^1)$, and we construct natural closed 2-forms $ω_β$ induced by the Atiyah-Bott construction. For non-integer $β$, the form $ω_β$ is symplectic, and one can identify $\rm{Teich}^β(\overline{\mathbb D})$ with the corresponding elliptic Virasoro coadjoint orbit. For positive integers $β=n$, $ω_β$ is presymplectic, and it descends to the Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau symplectic form on the exceptional Virasoro orbit $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)\backslash\rm{Diff}(S^1)$. Infinitesimal isometries of a hyperbolic \(0\)-metric on a disk with a conical singularity with angle $θ=2πn$ are given by the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb R)$ which integrates to the group $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)$ on the boundary of the disk but not in the interior for $n>1$. It is remarkable that the presymplectic structure of the corresponding Teichmüller spaces recovers this group and descends to the corresponding Virasoro coadjoint orbit.

candidates.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
candidates.abstract: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to the conformal bootstrap.

candidates.title: Holographic Spread Complexity of a Probe Particle with General Initial Data
candidates.abstract: We investigate the holographic spread complexity of a massive particle probing global AdS$_3$ with general initial data. By constructing an adapted Hamiltonian, we map each bulk geodesic to a boundary Krylov dynamical pair, whose dynamics are governed solely by the conserved chiral charges. We find that, for generic initial data, the original identification $\dot{C}\sim p_ρ$ fails; instead, both the complexity and its growth rate depend nonlinearly on the bulk Noether charges. We systematically analyze this nonlinear encoding via several perturbative expansions. We further investigate two refined variants: the symmetry-resolved spread complexity, which restores the bulk radial $π$-periodicity, and the chiral spread complexity, which admits an exact closed form approaching the standard complexity at small angular momentum. Finally, by directly quantizing an effective AdS$_2$ theory, we obtain a new holographic interpretation of spread complexity in terms of the lapse function.

candidates.title: The DBI critical electric field in stationary non-diagonal geometries
candidates.abstract: We investigate the critical electric field for the holographic Schwinger effect in general stationary non-diagonal geometries. We show that, in such backgrounds, the DBI reality condition must be formulated in terms of the electric field measured in a local orthonormal frame, since the coordinate components of the field strength need not represent a purely electric field in that frame. The critical field measured in the orthonormal frame takes the universal value \(E_{\mathrm{proper},c}=T_F\), while its coordinate expression depends on the background geometry. The resulting critical field is independently confirmed by the holographic potential analysis, through the disappearance of the potential barrier. We further illustrate the general prescription using the planar limit and the global rotating Myers--Perry--AdS geometry, which exhibit different types of metric mixing.

candidates.title: Holographic Entanglement Entropy of Network CFT
candidates.abstract: Miao et al. \cite{Guo:2025sbm, Guo:2026prm} proposed the AdS/NCFT correspondence, which explores the gravity dual of conformal field theories defined on networks. While previous studies investigated this model within Einstein and Gauss-Bonnet gravity (first- and second-order Lovelock gravity), in this paper, we generalize the framework to higher-order Lovelock gravity and more complex network structures. We derive the extremal and junction conditions for generalized Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) surfaces in third-order Lovelock gravity, which can be naturally extended to arbitrary higher-order Lovelock theories. Focusing on a network model comprising one node and three branches, we numerically investigate the relationship between the network holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and gravitational coupling coefficients. Furthermore, by analyzing the HEE across various network configurations, we find that the primary structural feature affecting the network HEE is the presence of internal nodes within line-shaped networks. Our results indicate that the network HEE decreases as the number or depth of internal branches increases.

candidates.title: M5-branes wrapped on topological disks from maximal 7D gauged supergravity
candidates.abstract: We study new supersymmetric $AdS_5 \times Σ$ solutions for $Σ$ being a topological disk from the maximal gauged supergravity in seven dimensions with $CSO(p,q,5-p-q)$ gauge groups. These gauged supergravities can be obtained from consistent truncations of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $H^{p,q} \circ T^{5-p-q}$. We find a number of solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ and $SO(3,2)$ gauge groups as well as $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetric solutions from $SO(5)$ and $SO(4,1)$ gauge groups. Solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetry preserve $16$ supercharges while the other solutions preserve only $8$ supercharges. Although some of the solutions give a holographic description of the dual $N=1$ SCFTs in four dimensions with finite central charges, most of the solutions describe codimension-2 defects within $N=(2,0)$ theories in six dimensions. For solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ gauge group for which a complete truncation ansatz of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $S^4$ is known, we also uplift the solutions to eleven dimensions and compute the holographic central charge of the dual four-dimensional $N=1$ SCFT with $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetry.

candidates.title: Quantum kernels on breast data: concentration, surrogates, and two ways an advantage gets manufactured
candidates.abstract: Quantum-kernel advantage claims on breast data are usually a single number: one quantum arm, one comparator, one test split. We asked what that number measures once the full comparator set and selection history are visible. We report three active benchmarks, all exact classical statevector simulations of 8-qubit fidelity kernels with no quantum component in the inference path: a sample-efficiency sweep on Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer at ten training-set sizes; raw-versus-processed arms on 1,200 M-SYNTH simulated mammograms with a matched closed-form dequantisation surrogate, five classical methods at the same input and eleven kernel families; and a 30-seed selection-inflation measurement on BreastMNIST. A CMMD D1 clinical arm is withdrawn as a result arm because its frozen splits leak the label through patient serial order, a defect reported in a separate study; it is retained only as a worked example. All three active arms are negative. On M-SYNTH raw an apparent +0.1736 (p = 5.2e-06) against a tuned RBF-SVM falls to +0.0019 (p = 0.937) against a random forest at the same input, and a Laplacian kernel wins on validation. On WDBC, with model selection confined to training data, the quantum kernel is below the selected classical arm at every training-set size, with 2 of 200 paired subsamples ahead. Best-of-30 seed selection adds +0.0210 on BreastMNIST. One result does not fit: at bandwidth 2pi the matched closed-form Gaussian surrogate failed to reproduce the M-SYNTH raw kernel (0.5410 against 0.7045, p = 6.3e-06). Comparator choice and selection each produce effects larger than any quantum-classical difference we measured; we give a reporting standard that removes both.

candidates.title: Cosmic ray protons from 40 GeV to 10 EeV due to star formation?
candidates.abstract: The formation of massive stars eventually results in supernovae explosions. Typical supernova remnants (SNRs) accelerate cosmic ray (CR) protons up to $E_{max-p} \sim 10$ TeV; the value of $E_{max-p}$ may reach $\sim 1$ EeV for the case of the hypernovae and/or for a sub-relativistic velocity of the SNR's shock wave. We show that the observable CR proton spectrum in the energy range between 40 GeV and 10 EeV is reasonably well described with a sum of three components that correspond to three distinct SNR populations. We consider two basic scenarios of CR origin: I) the supergalactic scenario assuming diffusion of the protons inside a magnetic field structure with the characteristic radius $H = 1-20$ Mpc and II. the cosmological scenario with the maximum redshift of the sources $z_{max} = 6$.

candidates.title: Phase-Space Shaping Due to Betatron Cooling in Wakefield Accelerators and the Onset of the Ion-Channel Laser
candidates.abstract: Plasma-based accelerators are beginning to employ relativistic beams with unprecedented charge and ultrashort durations. These dense driver beams can drive wakes even in high-density plasmas ( ≳ 10 19 cm − 3 ), where betatron radiation becomes increasingly important and begins to affect the dynamics of the accelerated beam. We show that betatron cooling leads to a strong structuring of the phase space of the beam. This gives rise to bunched, ring-like structures with positive radial position and momentum gradients, i.e., population inversion of the amplitude of oscillation. We derive the characteristic timescales for this process analytically and confirm our predictions with multidimensional particle-in-cell simulations. The radiation-dominated regime of beam dynamics fundamentally alters the acceleration process and produces self-structured beams; particle-in-cell simulations of the resulting beams show that it becomes unstable to the ion-channel laser and lead to exponential amplification of radiation.
